title: Explore Bhutan with FREE Taktsang Monastery Tour
highlights: Explore Bhutan's rich traditions with visits to ancient dzongs, vibrant markets, and sacred monasteries, capped with breathtaking treks through lush valleys.
Step into Bhutan’s second-oldest fortress-monastery, Punakha Dzong famed for its grand halls, intricate woodwork, and iconic location between two rivers.
Head to the 17th-century Drukgyel Dzong, a fortress that commemorates Bhutan’s victory over Tibet, with vistas of Mount Jomolhari in the background.
Ascend through lush pine forests to reach Tiger's Nest Monastery, where tales of Guru Rinpoche's flight on a tigress come alive.
overview: Embark on an unforgettable Bhutan tour weaving through the vibrant streets of Thimphu, the tranquil landscapes of Punakha and Gangtey, and culminating in the awe-inspiring hike to Paro Taktsang. This journey seamlessly blends tradition with modernity, offering a rich cultural experience against the backdrop of Bhutan's stunning natural beauty. This tour promises a tapestry of memories, connecting you deeply with the heart and soul of Bhutan.

know_before_you_go: Cancellation After Rescheduling: Clients who reschedule their tours or treks but later decide to cancel will be subject to our standard cancellation policy. Any rescheduling fees paid will be non-refundable.
Images are for representation purpose only.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

It is recommended that you purchase travel insurance. Please note that the travel insurance is not included in the package price.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: Upon your arrival at the New Jalpaiguri Railway Station or Bagdogra International Airport, get driven to Phuntsholing, passing by charming villages and lush tea gardens along the way. Once in Phuntsholing, check in to your hotel and relax for the day. Later, you can explore the Karbandi Monastery, offering panoramic views of the surrounding valleys, or stroll through the vibrant local markets before returning to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
days.desc: In the morning, check out and get driven to Thimphu after completing your immigration process in order to obtain a travel permit. En route, you'll also make a stop at Chukha dam. Once in Thimphu, check in to your hotel. Later, you can visit the Buddha Dordenma statue, standing at an impressive 177 feet. Additionally, you can take a stroll through the Royal Botanical Garden or explore the bustling Handicrafts Market to shop for souvenirs before returning to the hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, get driven for Thimphu sightseeing tour. Visit the National Memorial Chorten, a serene stupa built in honor of Bhutan’s third king. Next, explore the Motithang Takin Preserve, home to Bhutan’s unique national animal, the takin. Marvel at the grandeur of Tashichho Dzong, a historic fortress-monastery that features numerous temples, chapels, and shrines. Discover Bhutan’s rich culture and heritage at the Royal Textile Museum and the Simply Bhutan Museum. Later, get driven back to the hotel.

days.title: Transfer to Punakha via Dochula Pass | Punakha Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: After checking out, get driven to Punakha, passing through the serene Dochula Pass, where panoramic views of the mountains and fluttering prayer flags offer a peaceful atmosphere. Upon arriving in Punakha, visit Chimi Lhakhang, renowned for its unique fertility blessings. Continue to the iconic Punakha Dzong, a stunning fortress by the rivers, and the Punakha Suspension Bridge, offering picturesque views. Later, check in at your hotel in Punakha for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Paro | Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: After checking out, you'll be driven through scenic Bhutanese villages en route to Paro. Once in Paro, visit Rinpung Dzong, a majestic fortress-monastery that houses a collection of sacred artifacts and offers stunning views of the surrounding valley. Next, explore Nyamai Zam, an ancient wooden bridge with historical significance and picturesque views of the Paro Chhu river. Afterward, check in to your hotel & relax for the day.

days.title: Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
days.desc: Today, get driven to the base of the Taktsang Monastery, also known as Tiger’s Nest. Begin your 7-km trek through lush pine forests, with vibrant prayer flags fluttering in the breeze, leading you towards the monastery perched on a cliff. Explore the sacred site, home to meditation caves, ancient murals, and prayer wheels dedicated to Guru Rinpoche. After descending, you will be transferred back to your hotel for a restful night.
